title: Expiring reward points via link and card details vs. points-expiry notice
summary: A caller from Kaveri Bank tells the recipient that credit-card reward points are about to expire. In the fraud case, the caller sends a link, says the points expire today, and asks the recipient to enter their full card number, expiry date, and CVV on that page to convert the points to cash. In the legitimate case, the caller reminds the recipient that points expire at the end of the month and tells them to redeem in the Rewards section of the official app, and asks for nothing.

shared_setting.pretext: reward points worth about [AMOUNT_1] (₹1,000–₹12,000) are due to expire.
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult Kaveri Bank credit-card holder; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers say points can be converted to a statement credit or vouchers.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller directs the recipient to an unofficial link and asks for full card details, including the CVV, under a same-day deadline. Card details and CVV are enough to make card-not-present payments.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient's full card number, expiry date, and CVV entered on a look-alike page.
stable_facts: Link: https://kaveri-rewards-redeem.invalid/claim (sent by SMS during the call).
The page shows the bank's name and asks for card number, expiry, CVV, and then an OTP.

legitimate.label_rationale: The caller gives an expiry reminder and points to the official app. No link is sent and no card details are asked.
legitimate.caller_objective: Remind the recipient to redeem points before they expire.
stable_facts: Expiry: end of the current month, two to four weeks away.
Redemption: the Rewards section of the Kaveri Bank app the recipient already has, or the bank's website typed in by the recipient.
The caller says the bank never asks for card number, CVV, or OTP to redeem points.

cooperative.fraud: Opens the link and asks where the CVV is on the card
cooperative.legitimate: Says they will redeem in the app this weekend

clarifying.fraud: Asks why the bank's own app cannot be used
clarifying.legitimate: Asks whether points can be moved to the statement as cash

resistant.fraud: Says they will check in the app later and not open links
resistant.legitimate: Says they are not interested in the points

suspicious.fraud: Says the link does not look like the bank's and asks if this is phishing
suspicious.legitimate: Asks how they can know this call is really from the bank

fraud: caller pushes and recipient hangs up
recipient says they will call the number on the card.
legitimate: recipient is told to verify by calling the number on the back of the card.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may insist on the link, resend it, or raise urgency. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example an app install or payment to a UPI ID). The legitimate caller must not send a link or ask for any card detail after the branch.

must_preserve: card last-four and points value in both
app-only redemption and explicit "no card details" statement (_L)
may_vary: up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: real card numbers or CVV formats beyond a placeholder

ambiguities: Expire", "points", and "redeem" appear in both cases. The label depends on the link and the card-detail request.
Real campaigns of this type often ask users to install an app file from a message (CB14). This card uses a link and card details instead, so it does not overlap with the app-install families (bp_04).
The mechanism (unofficial link plus credentials under a deadline) is the same as bp_02 with a different pretext and credential. Deduplication should decide whether both stay.

evidence_references.claim: Banks never ask for card details, CVV, or OTP (C01)
Impostors cite "an attractive discount" or similar to get card credentials (C02)
Expiring-reward-points messages with app files or links are fake per PIB Fact Check (CB14)
